title: School lockdown
about: For staff at a New Zealand school or early learning service in a lockdown: alert, call 111, roll check, lock, stay inside, all-clear, reunite. Keeps the times.

steps.title: Told to lock down or shelter in place

An instruction can come from Police, the principal or delegate, the early childhood service manager or person responsible, other emergency services, or the Ministry of Education (at the direction of Police or another emergency service).

quotes.text: Instructions to shelter in place or lockdown may be initiated by:
the Ministry of Education (at the direction of the Police or other emergency service).

lines.text: If Police started it, they advise when it is lifted, through the principal or manager or through the Ministry.

quotes.text: If the Police initiated the shelter in place or lockdown, they would provide advice on lifting the shelter in place or lockdown directive through the principal or early childhood service manager directly or through the Ministry of Education.

lines.text: Lockdown: the threat is directly related to your school or centre, for example an attacker on your grounds.

quotes.text: Lockdown – issued when the threat is directly related to your school/centre.
For example, an attacker on your property/grounds.

lines.text: Shelter in place: the threat is external and not directed at you, for example wasps, toxic smoke, a chemical spill or an offender nearby.

quotes.text: Shelter in place – issued when the threat is external and not directed at your school/centre.
For example, if there is a swarm of wasps, toxic smoke, chemical spill, or a threat from an offender nearby

lines.text: If you made the decision, you lift it yourself.

quotes.text: If you made the decision to shelter in place or lockdown, you would lift the directive yourself.

No one should be allowed in or out of the grounds and buildings until the authorities give an all-clear signal.
Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems could be shut down if necessary (to prevent spread of harmful air) and doors and windows could be closed.

lines.text: Who collected each child

lines.text: A child who cannot be safely collected stays in your care until arrangements are made. A student going home alone needs support at home and a safe route; consider whether home is empty.

quotes.text: If for whatever reason, a child cannot be safely collected, the school or early childhood service will need to take responsibility for their care until appropriate arrangements are put in place.
You will need to ensure the student has appropriate support at home following an emergency event and they have a safe route home.

lines.text: Tell parents the lockdown has ended and you are resuming usual activities until the normal end of day.

lines.text: Ministry Traumatic Incident team, any time: 0800 848 326.

quotes.text: You can contact them at any time.
Freephone (NZ only): 0800 TI TEAM (0800 848 326)

lines.text: Traumatic Incident team contacted
Debriefs work well when led by people not directly involved. You could involve Police and invite the Ministry TI team. Share the key findings with staff, board, service providers and community.

quotes.text: Post-incident evaluation has been found to work well when it is led or coordinated by people not directly involved in the incident.
You could involve the Police to help you assess, and if involved, invite Ministry of Education Traumatic Incident Team members to participate.

lines.text: TI teams do not take over; they help your team respond. In bigger events you can ask for a team to come to you.

quotes.text: The Ministry TI teams do not take over and manage the incident for you; rather they can help your management team to respond.
